intro: Professionals and everyday users convert pound-inches (lb·in) to pound-feet (lb·ft) when working across imperial and imperial standards in automotive lug nut torque wrench settings, engine dynamometer curves, and industrial fastener specifications. One pound-inch (in·lbf) equals 0.083333 pound-feet, while 1 pound-foot (ft·lbf) equals 12 pound-inches. Whether you are verifying torque specifications on imported equipment, cross-checking technical datasheets, or scaling practical measurements, this converter applies the exact NIST SP 811 and ISO 80000 reference relationship with instant precision.

faqs.question: How many pound-feet (lb·ft) are in 1 pound-inch (in·lbf) (lb·in)?
faqs.answer: There are 0.08333333 pound-feet (lb·ft) in 1 pound-inch (in·lbf) (lb·in), which rounds to 0.0833 lb·ft for everyday calculations. Conversely, 1 pound-foot (ft·lbf) equals 12 pound-inches.

faqs.question: How do I convert pound-inches to pound-feet (lb·in to lb·ft)?
faqs.answer: To convert pound-inches to pound-feet, use the formula: lb·ft = lb·in × 0.08333333. For example, converting 50 lb·in gives 4.1667 lb·ft.

faqs.question: What is 50 pound-inches in pound-feet?
faqs.answer: 50 pound-inches (lb·in) equals exactly 4.1667 pound-feet (lb·ft) using standard NIST SP 811 and ISO 80000 conversion factors.
